cues.zh: 让我稍微谈谈
cues.en: Asked me to talk a little bit about the

cues.zh: 投票系统的新创新。所以我想跟你们讲讲端到端
cues.en: new innovations in voting systems. And so I'd like to tell you about end-to-end

cues.zh: 可验证的投票系统，
cues.en: verifiable voting systems,

cues.zh: 这是学术界用来描述它的流行术语。
cues.en: which is the buzzword that academics are using to describe this.

cues.zh: 也就是说，你确实可以验证整个信息流程，
cues.en: Now,Which means really that you can verify the whole flow of

cues.zh: 从你脑中决定想投给谁，
cues.en: information, from your head, as to who you think you want to vote for,

cues.zh: 一直到投出选票、计票
cues.en: all the way through the casting of the vote and the tabulation

cues.zh: 以及最终的统计结果，
cues.en: and then the final tally,

cues.zh: 这样你就能验证每一步都按应有的方式进行，
cues.en: so that you can verify that every step of the way is going the way it should

cues.zh: 你的选票按你的意愿被计算，
cues.en: and that your vote counts the way you intended,

cues.zh: 最终结果准确反映了所有人的投票。
cues.en: that the final result is the accurate representation of everybody's votes.

cues.zh: 目前，许多投票系统
cues.en: And right now, with many voting systems,

cues.zh: 都有一定程度的可验证性。纸质选票的好处在于
cues.en: you can have a certain amount of verifiability. The lovely thing about paper ballots

cues.zh: 你能看到，你写下的就是你的本意。所以这是一个
cues.en: is that you can see that, you know, what you wrote down is what you intended. And so that's a

cues.zh: 非常重要的特性，非常好。
cues.en: very important property, very nice.

cues.zh: 但一旦你投下纸质选票，你就得信任这些纸质选票的保管链
cues.en: But once you've cast the paper ballot, you're trusting the chain of custody of those paper ballots

cues.zh: 以确保计票正确无误
cues.en: to make sure that the count is done right

cues.zh: 并且被计数的选票是正确的那些。
cues.en: and that the ballots being counted are the right ones.

cues.zh: Brady：“跟我聊聊这个自拍的事。有些人喜欢拍自己选票的照片，对吧？”
cues.en: Brady: "Talk to me about this selfie thing. Some people like to take a photo of their ballot, don't they?"

cues.zh: 是的，这挺有意思的，而且我认为这可能会提高选民的参与度
cues.en: Yeah, it's a lot of fun, and I think it may increase voter participation

cues.zh: 在投票站里多一点这样的乐趣等等。
cues.en: to have a little more fun like that in the ballot booth and so on, too.

cues.zh: 不过，令人担忧的是，从
cues.en: The thing that is worrisome about it, though, from

cues.zh: 安全角度来看，你拍下自己投票的自拍，
cues.en: a security point of view, is that, you know, with a selfie of you casting your ballot,

cues.zh: 你就可以卖掉你的选票。这是我们几十年来艰难学到的教训之一，
cues.en: you can sell your ballot. And that's one of the things that we've learned the hard way over many many decades,

cues.zh: 就是你不能让人有机会出售他们的选票。
cues.en: is that you don't want to enable people to sell their ballots.

cues.zh: 所以你不能带着任何能证明你投票内容的凭证离开投票站。
cues.en: So you shouldn't leave the voting booth with any kind of proof as to how you voted.

cues.zh: 你不该拿到一张写着“我投了这个人”的收据，也不该拿到选票的副本，
cues.en: You shouldn't have a receipt saying you voted this way, you shouldn't have a copy of your ballot,

cues.zh: 你不该有任何能证明你投票内容的东西。
cues.en: you shouldn't have anything that proves how you voted.

cues.zh: 因为那可能值，你知道，20块钱，对你来说，
cues.en: Because that can be worth, you know, 20 bucks to the, you know, to you,

cues.zh: 酒吧里那个想买你选票的人愿意出这个价。或者可能是想胁迫你。
cues.en: from the guy down the bar who wants to, you know, buy your vote. Or maybe coerce you.

cues.zh: 那么，你怎么可能知道你的选票被按你的意愿计算了呢？
cues.en: So, yeah, how can you possibly know that your vote was counted the way you wanted?

cues.zh: 这是个难题，也构成了一个迷人的研究领域。而事实证明，
cues.en: This is a hard question, and it makes a fascinating research area. And it turns out

cues.zh: 只要稍加用心，再加上一点密码学、一点数学，你就能巧妙地解决这个难题。
cues.en: you can thread this needle with a bit of care and a bit of cryptography, a bit of mathematics.

cues.zh: 那具体怎么做呢？
cues.en: So how do you do this?

cues.zh: 思路是：你投票时会拿到一张收据。
cues.en: So the idea would be that you get a receipt when you vote.

cues.zh: 而回执并不是你投了谁的明文本
cues.en: And the receipt is not the plain text as to how you voted

cues.zh: 而是你投票内容的加密形式。所以这东西你没法拿到酒吧去卖，
cues.en: but an encryption of how you voted. So it's something that you can't sell down at the bar,

cues.zh: 因为别人没法解读它。
cues.en: because it's not something that's interpretable by somebody else.

cues.zh: Brady：“那它到底是什么，是个数字，还是条形码，还是……？”
cues.en: Brady: "So what is it, like a number, or a barcode, or...?"

cues.zh: 是个数字或条形码之类的。它代表了你投的票。
cues.en: It's a number or a barcode or something like that. It represents how you voted.

cues.zh: 所以你拿到一张回执，
cues.en: So you get a receipt,

cues.zh: 而这些端到端可验证系统的新之处在于
cues.en: and, the new thing here in these end-to-end verifiable systems

cues.zh: 所有回执的副本都会被发布到网上。
cues.en: is the copies of all the receipts get posted on the web.

cues.zh: 比如说，Brady，这是Brady的回执，还有Ron，这是Ron的回执，以此类推。每个人的名字和他们的
cues.en: So say, Brady, and here Brady's receipt, and Ron, and here's Ron's receipt, and so on and so forth. Everybody's name and their

cues.zh: 回执都会被发布出来。
cues.en: receipts get posted.

cues.zh: 没人能看出别人是怎么投的。你没法凭这份公示去卖选票。但它全都在网上，
cues.en: Nobody can tell how anybody else voted. You can't sell your vote based on that posting. But it's all on the web,

cues.zh: 全都摆在那儿，谁都能看。你可以去看，然后确认，没错，
cues.en: and it's all there for anybody look at. And you can look at it, and you can see that, yep,

cues.zh: 他们把我的回执弄对了，而那张回执就是我投票内容的加密，对吧？
cues.en: they've got my receipt right, and that receipt is an encryption of my vote, right?

cues.zh: 所以这是关键。你知道你的选票在票堆里，
cues.en: So that's the key thing. You know your vote is in the pile,

cues.zh: 而且你知道你的选票在票堆里，是按你认为正确的方式投的，
cues.en: and you know your vote is in the pile the way you think it should be,

cues.zh: 因为你有理由相信——我稍后会解释——
cues.en: because you have reason to believe, as I'll explain,

cues.zh: 你对选票的加密实际上是正确的。
cues.en: that your encryption of your vote is actually correct.

cues.zh: Brady：“不过每个人的加密看起来都不一样。”
cues.en: Brady: "Everyone's encryption looks different, though."

cues.zh: 每个人的加密看起来都不一样。
cues.en: Everybody's encryption looks different.

cues.zh: 所以这不是一种确定性的简单加密。这点说得好。
cues.en: So it's not a simple encryption in a deterministic way. It's a good point.

cues.zh: 对，所以如果大家都投给 Alice，所有投 Alice 的加密票看起来并不一样，所有投 Bob 的也不一样。
cues.en: Yeah, so if everybody's voting for Alice, all the Alices don't look the same, and all the Bobs don't look the same.

cues.zh: 所以这里有几个微妙之处。其一，那你怎么验证计票结果呢？有人宣布
cues.en: So there's a couple of subtleties here. One is, well, how do you verify the tally then? So somebody is announcing that

cues.zh: Alice 赢了。那么，所有这些加密选票
cues.en: Alice won. And so, all these encrypted votes are

cues.zh: 主要是投给 Alice 的，也有一些投给 Bob，但投给 Alice 的更多。
cues.en: primarily for Alice, and there's some for Bob, but there's more for Alice.

cues.zh: 这是选举官员做出的断言。他们怎么知道？他们如何
cues.en: That's the assertion that the election officials have made. How do they know? How do they

cues.zh: 说服任何人这是对的？他们想说服所有人这是对的，又不展示每个人选票的解密内容。
cues.en: convince anybody that that's right? And they'd like to convince everybody that that's right without showing the decryptions of everybody's vote.

cues.zh: 所以他们有一堆加密选票和一个公布的结果，
cues.en: So they've got this pile of encrypted votes and an announced result,

cues.zh: 你想知道……如果你是选举官员，你想说服所有人这是正确的结果。
cues.en: and you'd like to know,... if you're an election official, you'd like to convince everybody that's the right result.

cues.zh: 有很多方法可以做到这一点，相关文献也相当多。这里有一种
cues.en: So there's a number of ways of doing this, and there's quite a large literature on this. Here's a way

cues.zh: 描述起来相当简单的方法。你可以使用一种叫做同态加密的东西。
cues.en: that's pretty simple to describe. So you could use something called homomorphic encryption.

cues.zh: 那是什么意思？意思是你可以把
cues.en: What does that mean? So it means that you can multiply

cues.zh: 密文相乘，得到的结果代表它们明文的和。
cues.en: ciphertext together and end up with them representing the sum of their plaintext.

cues.zh: 所以，对1的加密和对2的加密相乘，就会得到对3的加密，对吧？
cues.en: So, encryption of a one times an encryption of a two will give you an encryption of a three, right?

cues.zh: 所以，当你把密文相乘时，实际上是在把明文相加。这很酷。
cues.en: So you end up adding the plaintext when you multiply the ciphertext. So this is cool.

cues.zh: 你可以用这个做很多奇妙的事情。特别是，你可以用它来为投票系统计票。
cues.en: You can do lots of wonderful things with this. And in particular, you can do the tally for the voting system.

cues.zh: 例如，如果你的票是投给Alice的，你可能有一个对1的加密。
cues.en: For example, if your vote is a vote for Alice, you might have an encryption of a one.

cues.zh: 如果你的票是投给Bob的，你可能有一个对0的加密。假设Alice和Bob是仅有的两位候选人。
cues.en: And if your vote is a vote for Bob, you might have an encryption for a zero. And suppose Alice and Bob are the only two candidates.

cues.zh: 那么，每张选票要么是1要么是0，基本上你要做的就是把它们加起来。
cues.en: So then, each ballot is either a one or a zero, and basically what you want to do is add them up.

cues.zh: 但它们是密文，所以你看不到那些1和0。
cues.en: But they're ciphertexts, so you don't see the ones and the zeros.

cues.zh: 但你可以利用这个同态性质，把所有密文相乘
cues.en: But you can use this homomorphic property, you can multiply all these ciphertexts together

cues.zh: 最终得到一个数，它代表所有
cues.en: end up with a number which represents the sum of all of the

cues.zh: 明文选票的总和。那么这个总和就是投给Alice的票数，对吧？
cues.en: plaintext ballots. And that sum is just the number of votes cast for Alice then, right?

cues.zh: Alice 的得票总数就是所有这些的总和。而 Bob 的得票数就是总票数减去 Alice 的得票总数，
cues.en: So the tally for Alice is the sum of all these things. And Bob is just the number of votes minus the tally for Alice,

cues.zh: 当然。所以如果 Alice 得票超过半数，她就赢了。
cues.en: of course. So if Alice has more than half, she wins.

cues.zh: 所以在这里，你可以把这些密文相乘，得到一个密文，它就是总和对应的密文，
cues.en: So there, you can multiply these ciphertexts together and get a ciphertext that's the ciphertext for the sum,

cues.zh: 而且这个密文可以被公开解密，
cues.en: and that ciphertext can be decrypted publicly

cues.zh: 以所有人都能看出是正确的方式。所以你能看到，是的，那就是……而且每个人也都能做这个乘法，
cues.en: in a way that everybody can see is proper. So you can see yes that is... and everybody could also do this multiplication,

cues.zh: 也就是说，他们可以检查那就是要解密的密文，
cues.en: So that is, they can check that that's the ciphertext to decrypt,

cues.zh: 选举官员可以用一种妥当的方式解密它，
cues.en: and the election officials could decrypt that in a nice way

cues.zh: 并证明那是正确的解密结果，这样我们就能得到 Alice 的正确得票总数。
cues.en: and show that that's the proper decryption, so that we have the right tally for Alice.

cues.zh: 所以这就是你需要做的一部分，也就是每个人都能从这些加密内容中验证得票总数。
cues.en: So that's one part of what you need to do then, is everybody can verify the tally from these encrypted things.

cues.zh: 这很酷，对吧？这是其中一部分。另一部分你需要
cues.en: And that's cool, right? So that's one part of it. The other part you want to

cues.zh: 处理的是，你需要知道你的密文确实代表了你的选票，对吧？所以你走进
cues.en: deal with is the fact that you need to know that your ciphertext is really representing your vote, right? So you go into the

cues.zh: 投票亭，你拿到这张回执，
cues.en: voting booth, you're getting this receipt,

cues.zh: 你想知道这张回执确实代表了你的选票。所以你投给 Alice，然后你拿到这张回执，它是一个
cues.en: and you want to know that that receipt really represents your vote. So you vote for Alice, and you get this receipt which is a

cues.zh: 密文，
cues.en: ciphertext,

cues.zh: 你无法解密那个密文。事实上，你就不应该能解密那个
cues.en: you can't decrypt that ciphertext. In fact, you shouldn't be able to decrypt that

cues.zh: 密文，因为那样你就可以卖掉你的选票，就像你自拍那样，对吧？所以你想知道那个
cues.en: ciphertext, because then you could sell your vote, just like you could with a selfie, right? So you want to know that that

cues.zh: 密文确实是投给，比如说，Alice 的，如果你投给 Alice 的话。
cues.en: ciphertext is really for, say, Alice, if you're voting for Alice.

cues.zh: 所以，这就更微妙一些。
cues.en: So, that's a little more subtle.

cues.zh: 也许火柴盒这个类比用来解释还不赖。你怎么
cues.en: Maybe this matchbox analogy is not a bad way to explain it. How do you

cues.zh: 知道你有了一根好火柴？你要去露营，你只能，你只被允许带一根火柴
cues.en: know that you've got a good match? You're going on a camping trip, you can, you're allowed to take only one match

cues.zh: 你怎么知道你有了一根好火柴？
cues.en: How do you know you've got a good match?

cues.zh: 你可以从抽屉里拿出一个盒子，然后说，
cues.en: Well, you could take a box out of the drawer, you can say well,

cues.zh: 也许这是一盒好火柴。
cues.en: maybe this is a box of good matches.

cues.zh: 你随机抽取那些火柴试一下，点亮，嗯，这根着了，那根也着了。
cues.en: And you try randomly sampling those matches, and, light, yeah, that one lights, that one lights.

cues.zh: 但你想带一根还没试过的火柴走。于是你，
cues.en: But you want to take with you a match you haven't tried yet. And so you,

cues.zh: 也许是最后一根，你说，嗯，这根我还没试过，但盒子里其他所有的都是好的，因此
cues.en: maybe the last match, you say, well, I haven't tried that match, but all the others in the box were good, and therefore

cues.zh: 我相信这根也是好的。你把它放进口袋，带去露营。
cues.en: I'm going to trust that this one is good. You put that your pocket and take it camping.

cues.zh: 在这里的加密中，你也可以做类似的事情。你可以说，我走进投票 booth，
cues.en: So you can do something like that with the encryption here. You can say, I walk into the voting booth,

cues.zh: 我得到我第一个
cues.en: I get an encryption of my first

cues.zh: 选择的表示的加密。我说 Alice，然后得到加密，接着我想看看，
cues.en: representation of the choice. I say Alice and I get encryption, then I want to see,

cues.zh: 这真的是一个好的加密吗？就像看看这是不是一根好火柴。
cues.en: is that really a good encryption? It's like seeing if it's a good match.

cues.zh: 那我就把它作废，或者我要求把它解密，
cues.en: So I'll strike it, or I'll ask that to be decrypted,

cues.zh: 这个机器可以帮我做到，因为它
cues.en: which the machine can do for me, since it

cues.zh: 一开始就是它加密的。所以，一旦我测试了，一旦我看到它是如何正确解密的，可惜的是，
cues.en: encrypted it in the first place. So, so once I test it, I, once I see that, how it decrypts properly, unfortunately,

cues.zh: 我不能用那个来投票，因为现在我也知道它是怎么解密的了，
cues.en: I can't use that to vote with, because now I know how to, how it decrypts as well,

cues.zh: 而且我不能把它公布出去，因为要是公布出去，我就能卖掉我的选票。
cues.en: and I can't post that, because I could sell my vote if I were to post that one.

cues.zh: 所以那就是一张废票，我们不能用它。
cues.en: So that's a spoiled ballot, and, and we can't use that.

cues.zh: Brady：“那个会被从计票中剔除。”
cues.en: Brady: "That gets taken off the tally."

cues.zh: 它会被拿走，甚至不会被公布，
cues.en: It's taken, it's not even posted,

cues.zh: 它不在计票中，不会被使用，哪里都没有它。就像我根本没投过票一样，
cues.en: it's not in the tally, it's not used, it's not anywheres. It's like I haven't voted at all,

cues.zh: 我只是在测试投票机。而且我想做多少次都行，你知道，两三次，
cues.en: I'm just testing the voting machine. And I can do that as many times as I like, you know, two or three times,

cues.zh: 看看不同内容的不同解密结果，我就能看出这台机器可靠地加密了
cues.en: check out different decryptions of different things, and I can see the machine is reliably encrypting

cues.zh: 我说我想投给谁的内容。我可以说我投给 Alice 并测试一下，我可以说我投给 Bob 再测试一下，
cues.en: whatever I say I want to vote for. I can say I'm voting for Alice and test that, I can say I'm voting for Bob and I test that,

cues.zh: 然后再说我投给 Alice。也许那个我就不测试了，我说，好，就用这个吧，
cues.en: and say I'm voting for Alice again. Maybe I don't test that one, and I say, okay we'll go with that,

cues.zh: 我们把它公布到网上。然后你就有信心了，就像那些火柴一样，那个加密是正确完成的。
cues.en: we'll post that on the web. And then you've got confidence, just like with the matches, that that encryption was done properly.

cues.zh: 不需要很多人来做，对吧？只需要做得足够充分
cues.en: It doesn't need to be done by a lot of people, right? It just needs to be done enough

cues.zh: 让你知道机器不会大规模地作弊。
cues.en: so that you know machines aren't trying to cheat in any large-scale way.

cues.zh: 这就是它的两个部分。获得你可以信任的加密，即使你不是计算机，
cues.en: So those are the two parts of it. Getting encryptions that you can trust, even if you're not a computer,

cues.zh: 并获得你可以验证的计票结果，尽管计票的输入是加密的。
cues.en: and getting a tally that you can verify, even though the inputs of the tally are encryptions.

cues.zh: 所以这是一个绝妙的想法。多年来，许多人不断完善它
cues.en: And so this is a wonderful idea. It's evolved over the years with many different people

cues.zh: 把各部分拼在一起，但这意味着你可以拥有一个投票系统，
cues.en: putting parts of it together, but it means you can have a voting system, then,

cues.zh: 它是可验证的，从你想投票给谁，那个流程的末端开始，
cues.en: that's verifiable, all the way from who you want to vote for, that end of the process,

cues.zh: 经过投票、公布选票、计票和宣布结果。你可以验证
cues.en: through the casting of the ballot, through the posting of the ballots, through the tally and the announcement of the result. You can verify that the

cues.zh: 结果是正确的。所以，在未来，这可能会是那种
cues.en: outcome is right. So, in the future, this might be the kind of voting system

cues.zh: 所有人都将使用的投票系统。但它还处于研究阶段。还在开发中。
cues.en: everybody will vote on. But it's still in research stages a bit. It's under development.

cues.zh: 有些司法辖区已经开始实际使用，我们看看效果如何。我持乐观态度。
cues.en: There are some jurisdictions that are starting to use it in practice, and we'll see how it goes. I'm optimistic.
